chapter_theme: The vision of the downward face (அதோமுக தெரிசனம்): Siva's sixth face, turned downward, sent the six-faced Skanda against the asura, bears the cosmos and its quarters, and is the Lord of the aeon and the endless Shakti; his dark throat has a meaning that those who say 'he drank poison' miss.
structure_note: A narrative verse (520), three on the dark throat and the Lord's knowledge of the false (521, 522), and three dense verses that repeat அதோமுகம் (523 to 525).

520.reading: When the gods, their flowers blooming, cried 'Our great Lord, our God, is this just?' and told of the asura's might, the Supreme said to the six-faced one of beautiful coral body, 'go and kill their enemy.'
520.nuance: The chapter title links this to the downward face; tradition says Skanda was born from it. The verse itself names only the six-faced one and the command.

521.reading: No one knows the meaning of the darkened throat of the downward face that bears the cosmos and the eight directions; those without understanding say that what he ate was poison, of him who wears a garland of white skulls and spreading matted hair.
521.nuance: The verse does not deny the poison story outright; it says the story is what people without understanding tell. What the throat means instead is left unstated: tradition reads it as the Lord's holding of the world within.

522.reading: He who made them knows the men of the sea-girt world who praise with lies; if they spoke the truth, he of the throat dark and gleaming would make the gods worship them.
522.nuance: The falsehood may be false praise of the Lord or false speech in general. The reward for truth is put high: the gods themselves would bow.

523.reading: Nandi rising, high in the middle, mingled with the red fire, stands within as Siva; mingling first, he goes round the world; the Lord of the twilight is the downward face.
523.nuance: நடுவுற ஓங்கிய (rising in the middle) and செந்தீ (red fire) suggest a yogic ascent through the central channel; அந்தி (twilight) may be the juncture of day and night or of the breaths. All of this is tradition's reading.

524.reading: The downward face is the Ancient who is the lower cosmos; with the downward face he works everywhere; the Lord with the bright flower wreath of the hundred faces is also the downward-faced one, the Lord of the aeon.
524.nuance: சதோமுகம் is unclear: perhaps 'hundred-faced', or a form of சதாமுகம். ஊழித் தலைவன் (Lord of the aeon) links the face to dissolution.

525.reading: Hear how the downward face became the great flower: by the downward face it spread out a hundredfold; the endless Shakti that became the downward face, he became the downward face and abides.
525.nuance: The repetition of அதோமுகம் in every line is deliberate. The flower that opens a hundredfold may be a lotus of the body or of the cosmos; the verse identifies the face with Shakti and with Siva at once.

links.note: 524 makes the downward face the lower cosmos and the Lord of the aeon; 525 makes it the flower that opens a hundredfold and the endless Shakti.

Tirumanthiram 520 has the gods cry 'எம்பெருமான் இறைவா முறையோ', our Lord, is this just?, and the Supreme send the six-faced one to kill their enemy. Thiruppugazh 847 praises Murugan who threw the vel at old Sura 'முநிவோர் அமரோர் முறையோ எனவே', when the sages and gods cried 'is this just?'. The same cry of முறையோ starts the war in both; the Tirumanthiram tells it from Siva's command, the song from Murugan's vel.

339 says that when the gods begged ('வானவர் வேண்ட') because an asura was tormenting the world's lives, the Lord took the trident and killed him himself. 520 has the gods appeal in the same way about an asura's might, but the Supreme sends the six-faced one: 'தம்பகை கொல் என்ற'. The two follow the same pattern of the gods' plea and the asura's death; 520 gives the act to Murugan at Siva's command.

521 says no one knows the meaning of the darkened throat, and that 'உண்டது நஞ்சு என்று உரைப்பர் உணர்விலோர்', those without understanding say what he ate was poison. 2688 says that to take the poison from the salt sea 'ஆரமுதாக', as nectar, is the intent of the Lord with the shining throat. Both refuse the plain story of the poison: 2688 makes it nectar, and 521 makes the dark throat a sign of something else.

Kural 295 ranks one who speaks truth with the whole mind above those who do tapas and give gifts. Tirumanthiram 522 says the Lord knows the men who praise with lies, and that 'மெய்யே உரைக்கில்', if they spoke truth, he would make the gods worship them. Both set truthful speech above the acts usually praised; the Tirumanthiram makes truth the price of the highest honour and false praise of the Lord its failure.
